column7: Imagine a master sculptor preparing to work with a large block of marble. The master imagines what this raw and unshaped marble can be transformed into through his careful craftsmanship. He has a very specific design in mind, he orders his assistants to set this block of marble aside for a special design (**consecration**). As he refines and works the marble, adding texture, depth, and shape, he purifies it (**sanctifies**) for that special design. The act of dedicating the marble for his special project was quick, whereas the process of shaping the marble into its final design takes considerable patience.
column8: Imagine that a master sculptor is preparing to work with a large piece of white stone. This master envisions what this raw and shapeless stone could become through his careful craftsmanship. With a very specific design in mind, he tells his assistants to set this piece of stone aside for a particular design (**dedication**). As he refines and carves the stone, giving it layers, depth, and shape, he purifies it for that specific design (**sanctifies it**). The act of dedicating the stone to his special project was swift, but the process of shaping the stone into its final design requires considerable patience.
